items.title: AI-Based Detection of Hallucinated Outputs in Chatbots Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Review and Conceptual Framework
items.abstract: Chatbots based on Large Language Models (LLMs) can provide quick, fluent, and informative answers, but they sometimes generate incorrect or unsupported information known as hallucinations. These hallucinations can reduce user trust and create problems in areas such as education, healthcare, research, and customer support. Therefore, detecting and preventing hallucinated outputs is important for developing reliable and trustworthy AI systems. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a useful approach that retrieves relevant information from trusted sources before generating an answer. This retrieved information can be used to check whether the chatbot's response is accurate and supported by available evidence. However, RAG alone cannot completely prevent hallucinations because the generated answer may still contain incorrect facts, irrelevant information, or unsupported statements. This paper proposes a conceptual framework for detecting hallucinations in chatbot responses by combining information retrieval, evidence-based verification, and rule-based validation. The system compares the generated answer with retrieved information and identifies statements that are incorrect or lack sufficient supporting evidence. Based on the verification results, the system classifies the response as reliable or flagged. If the response contains unsupported information, the system can suggest corrections or prevent the answer from reaching the user without proper verification. The proposed approach aims to improve answer accuracy, reduce misleading information, and increase transparency in AI-based conversational systems. Although this framework offers a promising direction, its effectiveness depends on the quality of retrieved information, verification methods, and decision thresholds. Future evaluation should measure detection accuracy, response time, and computational cost. This approach can support the development of safer, more reliable, and trustworthy chatbots across different application areas.

items.title: AI-Based Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models Learning: A Review
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can produce fluent but incorrect or fabricated statements, called hallucinations, which limits their use in education, healthcare and other high-stakes areas. Most existing safeguards act only after generation, and few correct errors automatically. This paper presents a structured narrative review of [N] verified sources published between [2022] and 2026, organized into seven themes: taxonomies, sampling-consistency detection, semantic-clustering methods, retrieval and fact-verification, internal-state detection, correction and integrated architectures, and evaluation practices. Black-box methods can detect hallucinations without external knowledge or model access, but only 8.8 % of reviewed systems combine detection and mitigation. Evidence relies heavily on question-answering benchmarks, small datasets, automatically generated labels and non-comparable metrics, and correction layers are rarely validated. The paper contributes a thematic synthesis, a comparison of [N] studies, a conceptual seven-layer self-correcting architecture and a prioritized research agenda.

items.title: AI-Based Intelligent Medical Report Understanding and Personal Health Management System
items.abstract: Medical reports contain important health information, but their technical terminology and numerical results may be difficult for patients to understand. Recent studies have explored the use of large language models to simplify radiology reports, while also identifying concerns related to accuracy, omitted information, and potentially misleading explanations [1–3]. This paper proposes an AI-Based Intelligent Medical Report Understanding and Personal Health Management System designed to make medical information easier to understand and organize. The proposed framework will accept medical reports in PDF or image format, extract relevant text, and generate patient-friendly explanations while aiming to preserve important values, units, and reference ranges. A retrieval-based component is proposed to support explanations using reliable medical sources. Additional planned features include date-wise health-record organization, comparison of comparable report values, and reminders based on user-entered or clinician-provided instructions. The framework emphasizes privacy, factual consistency, and the distinction between educational information and professional medical advice. Its evaluation will examine text-extraction accuracy, preservation of medical information, factual consistency, readability, and usability after implementation. As the system has not yet been experimentally evaluated, this paper presents the proposed design and evaluation plan rather than measured performance results.

items.title: AI-Based Solar Power Forecasting and Health Monitoring Techniques: Recent Trends and Challenges
items.abstract: Solar energy has emerged as one of the most promising renewable energy sources due to its sustainability, abundance, and environmental benefits. However, the intermittent nature of solar power generation and system reliability challenges necessitate accurate forecasting and effective health monitoring techniques. Artificial Intelligence (AI), including Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL), has significantly transformed solar energy systems by improving forecasting accuracy, fault detection, predictive maintenance, and energy storage optimization. This review paper explores recent advancements in AI-based solar power forecasting and health monitoring techniques, emphasizing models such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and hybrid frameworks. The study also examines AI-driven predictive maintenance approaches, including IoT-based monitoring, digital twin technologies, and thermal imaging methods for photovoltaic systems and battery energy storage systems. Furthermore, recent trends such as explainable AI, reinforcement learning, and smart grid integration are discussed. The paper highlights key challenges, including data quality, computational complexity, model generalization, and real-time deployment, while identifying future opportunities for intelligent and scalable solar energy management systems.

items.title: AI-Driven Phishing Email Detection: A Comparative Review of Ensemble Learning, Explainable AI, and Stylometric Analysis
items.abstract: Phishing email remains a persistent cybersecurity threat, and large language models (LLMs) now allow fluent phishing text tobe produced at scale. This paper is a focused, literature-based comparative review of three recent studies that approach phishing emaildetection from different directions: a soft-voting ensemble with explainable-AI error analysis, a TF-IDF/SVM web platform with LIMEexplanations, and a stylometric classifier evaluated on GPT-4o-generated phishing emails alongside commercial spam filters. The studiesare compared by objective, dataset, feature family, model, evaluation protocol, reported metrics, explainability and stated limitations.Because the studies use different corpora and protocols, their reported figures are presented with attribution and are not ranked. Thecomparison suggests that content/structural detectors and stylometric detectors have been evaluated on largely disjoint data, so whethereither generalizes across conventional and AI-generated phishing is an open question raised by this review, not a verified research gap.The paper proposes a conceptual, unvalidated workflow that combines header/content/URL features, stylometric features, an ensembleclassifier and LIME-based analyst review, and specifies a future experimental protocol with hypotheses, cross-dataset tests and ablations.No new experimental results are reported.

items.title: AI-DRIVEN, EVIDENCE-BASED GENERATIVE DESIGN: A TEACHING FRAMEWORK FOR LANDSCAPE ARCHITECTONICS INTEGRATING RESEARCH FINDINGS, DESIGN PRECEDENTS, AND INTELLIGENT RECOGNITION AND JUDGMENT
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has entered design courses, but its use often stops at tool operation. Taking Landscape Architectonics, an undergraduate course in landscape architecture programs, as the vehicle, this paper builds a teaching framework for generative design that integrates four elements: research findings, design precedents, AI-based recognition and judgment, and AI generation. The core claim is simple. Teaching students to “use AI” means teaching them to run an evidence-constrained generative design chain. “AI-driven” therefore carries two meanings: at the tool level, AI executes generation; at the teaching level, evidence steers generation, and the work of teaching lies in leading students from the former toward the latter. Among the four elements, research findings and design precedents are static knowledge that travels across sites. Research findings supply criteria for what counts as good. Design precedents supply examples of what to do, distilled from 13 street design guidelines into 114 retrievable situation packages. AI-based recognition and AI generation produce dynamic outputs anchored to a specific site. Students mobilize these elements through three stages—reading the site, grounding the context, and giving form—and a chain of evidence disciplines each stage. The framework follows three design principles: complementary elements, partial embedding, and explicit judgment. Three classroom examples show how the framework operates. This paper focuses on framework construction and does not report learning-outcome data.

This critical review examines how measurement-while-drilling and logging while drilling information can support drilling rate optimisation adaptive well planning and predictive wellbore risk management within Saudi oil and gas operations. Thirty peer-reviewed publications issued between 2020 and 2025 were assessed through a structured, question led synthesis.The evidence was organized around measurement integrity, formation interpretation, optimisation architecture, trajectory revision, hazard prediction and deployment assurance. Published studies demonstrate substantial progress in rate - of - penetration forecasting, activity-aware influx detection and integrated geological-engineering planning. Nevertheless, model performance is generally assessed within particular fields or datasets; prospective validation, uncertainty calibration and evidence of avoided incidents remain less developed. The review proposes a bounded, human-supervised decision architecture in which physics-based constraints, data-quality controls and explicit operational authorisation separate algorithmic recommendations from drilling actions.

items.title: AI-Generated Fashion Imagery and Consumer Purchase Intention
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is widely adopted in fashion visual communication, yet imagery over-optimization causes product-image discrepancies and undermines consumer decisions. This study deconstructs three core characteristics of artificial intelligence-generated fashion imagery—visual realism, detail completeness, and style compatibility—and tests their impact on purchase intention via perceived authenticity and trust, with product price and consumer heterogeneity as moderators. Using a mixed-method approach (N = 845) and structural equation modeling, results confirm (1) the three characteristics positively influence purchase intention through direct risk reduction and indirect value identification, (2) trust plays dual mediating roles (direct and serial: artificial intelligence imagery → authenticity → trust → purchase intention), and (3) trust's mediation strengthens with higher prices (66.0% for high-price versus 39.6% for low-price products), and consumer segments differ in trust-building paths. This research enriches decision support system literature and offers actionable strategies for fashion brands.

items.title: AI-generated high-intensity interval training information: a cross-sectional comparative evaluation of quality and readability
items.abstract: Background AI chatbots are increasingly used for health and exercise information. High-intensity interval training (HIIT) is a common exercise topic, yet the quality, transparency, and readability of chatbot-generated HIIT information have not been systematically compared under a standardized testing protocol. Objective To compare selected dimensions of quality, transparency, and readability in HIIT-related responses generated by ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, and Perplexity, and to evaluate readability against a prespecified sixth-grade benchmark for public-facing health information. Methods This cross-sectional comparative content analysis was conducted in August 2026. Google Trends was used to identify HIIT-related search terms worldwide over the preceding 5 years. Of 29 candidate terms, 14 were retained after predefined screening, and each term was submitted once to each of four chatbots, yielding 56 responses. Two reviewers, both holding doctoral degrees in sports science, independently evaluated all responses using DISCERN, EQIP, the JAMA benchmark criteria, and GQS, which assessed complementary dimensions of information quality, usability, transparency, and overall usefulness. Inter-rater reliability was assessed before adjudication. Six readability indices were calculated. Because the same 14 queries were evaluated across all four chatbots, overall differences were tested using Friedman tests; significant results were followed by paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm correction. Kendall’s W was reported as the overall effect-size measure. Results Perplexity-generated responses had the highest median scores for DISCERN [51.50 (47.50, 53.75)], EQIP [75.00 (70.00, 80.00)], JAMA [1.00 (1.00, 1.00)], and GQS [4.00 (4.00, 4.00)]. Friedman tests showed significant differences across chatbots for DISCERN (χ 2 = 27.98, p < 0.001, W = 0.666), EQIP (χ 2 = 25.74, p < 0.001, W = 0.613), JAMA (χ 2 = 35.40, p < 0.001, W = 0.843), and GQS (χ 2 = 21.15, p < 0.001, W = 0.504). None of the four chatbots met the prespecified sixth-grade readability benchmark across the evaluated indices. Conclusion Under this specific testing protocol, HIIT-related responses generated by the four chatbots differed in the evaluated dimensions of information quality and transparency, with Perplexity-generated responses receiving higher median scores on all four assessment instruments. These scores should not be interpreted as direct evidence of factual accuracy, citation accuracy, or clinical safety, which were not independently assessed. None of the evaluated chatbot-generated responses met the prespecified readability benchmark.

items.title: AI-guided optimization and cradle-to-gate sustainability assessment of eco-friendly UHPC with supplementary cementitious materials and nano-additives
items.abstract: This study proposes an explainable artificial intelligence (AI)-guided framework for predicting compressive strength (CS) and assessing the sustainability of ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) mixtures incorporating supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs), nano-additives, and sustainable waste-derived constituents. A database containing 1990 experimental records of 28-day CS was compiled from the literature. Three tree-based machine learning algorithms, namely Extra Trees Regressor (ETR), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM), together with stacked ensemble models, were developed and optimized using the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA). Based on outcomes, among all developed models, the SM-4 (XGB+ETR+LGBM) model achieved the best overall testing performance with an R² of 0.885, RMSE of 12.40 MPa, MAE of 8.80 MPa, MAPE of 5.94%, and RMSRE of 8.37%. SHAP analyses identified curing temperature, fiber dosage, silica fume content, cement dosage, and water content as the most influential predictors. Cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA)-based analyses further evaluated carbon emissions, embodied energy, and material cost. Additionally, a multi-objective inverse-design framework coupled the best-performing stacked model with NSGA-II and TOPSIS to identify UHPC mixture proportions for eight CS targets from 130 to 200 MPa while considering sustainability indicators and mixture-design requirements. Selected mixtures were produced and experimentally tested to compare measured CS with predictions and prescribed targets. Finally, an AI-guided graphical user interface (GUI) was developed for rapid CS prediction and sustainability assessment. The proposed framework integrates interpretable prediction, sustainability assessment, and multi-objective optimization to identify UHPC mixtures for prescribed strength targets, with experimental validation supporting practical mixture-design applications.

items.title: AI-Powered Predictive Women Safety Ecosystem with Real-Time Audio Threat Detection: A Review
items.abstract: Women's safety is still an everyday concern in public places, workplaces and homes, and most tools in use today depend on the victim pressing a button at the worst possible moment. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers another route: listening for distress in the surroundings, combining it with other signals, and forecasting where and when the risk is highest. This paper reviews 15 IEEE-published sources from 2014 to 2024 that relate to this idea. They cover IoT-based safety devices, scream and distress detection from audio, speech emotion and fear recognition, multimodal wearable systems, crime hotspot prediction, and edge and privacy-preserving deployment. The review finds that the audio models report accuracies between 92% and 100% on the datasets they were tested on, while the one multimodal wearable study that tested fear recognition on unseen subjects reached 63.61%. Crime-prediction methods are mature at city level but are rarely linked to women-specific incidents or to live sensing. Most studies rely on small, public or acted data, say little about false alarms, response delay and battery use, and give limited attention to privacy, accents and noisy streets. The paper contributes a comparison of eleven representative works, a conceptual seven-layer architecture that joins on-device audio detection with predictive risk analytics, and a prioritised list of research gaps. The architecture is conceptual and has not been tested experimentally.

items.title: Algorithmic Pressure and Psycho-Emotional Risk Among Airport Employees: A Two-Level Mamdani Fuzzy Model
items.abstract: This study revealed that the growing use of intelligent algorithms in air transport and airport management alters the workload of airport employees and creates new psycho-emotional risks. High information-flow density, opaque algorithmic solutions, discrepancies between digital instructions and the actual situation, and limited professional autonomy and responsibility for process safety were identified as the main sources of psycho-emotional stress, particularly among airport employees exposed to algorithmic management and digital monitoring. These factors were found to jointly reduce personnel concentration and situational awareness, slow decision-making, increase professional stress, and raise the likelihood of erroneous actions. Proposed solutions for reducing psycho-emotional stress arising from aviation human–AI interaction were analyzed using results from past and ongoing projects in Europe, Singapore, and China. The feasibility of alleviating the psycho-emotional risks experienced by airport employees through self-adaptive technologies for algorithmic air transport management was substantiated. These technologies include explainable algorithmic recommendations, adaptive workload distribution, maintenance of human control, monitoring for signs of overload, and a regulated ability to deviate from control algorithms when the operational situation changes. The findings can guide the design of human-centered cognitive-adaptive management systems for airport operations and help develop organizational measures to preserve the professional well-being of aviation personnel.

items.title: ALLMTS: Automated LLM-based Medical Triage System
items.abstract: Telephone triage is a safety critical task: from a brief intake note, a nurse must decide whether a caller needs an ambulance, an emergency department, an appointment, or self care at home. Queried directly, large language models (LLMs) are unreliable: they over-escalate routine cases and cannot justify their recommendations against an auditable clinical standard. We present the Automated LLM-based Medical Triage System (ALLMTS), which grounds every disposition in the same commercially maintained telehealth guidelines nurses use. Rather than asking an LLM to triage, ALLMTS makes it execute the guideline: it selects the appropriate guideline and evaluates its triage assessment questions. The disposition follows deterministically from the first positive answer, using the same traversal rule a nurse follows. We evaluate ALLMTS on 566 synthetic, expert-validated scenarios spanning 14 dispositions and designed to test specific guideline questions. ALLMTS achieves 0.95 accuracy, compared with 0.47 for a raw-LLM baseline. On a curated 50-scenario subset released as an open benchmark, ALLMTS reaches 0.98 accuracy, on par with the 0.944 correct disposition rate that a five nurse expert panel recorded on those same scenarios. Critically, on that subset the baselines have over-triage rates of up to 0.50 (0.44 on the full dataset), whereas ALLMTS reduces the over-triage rate to at most 0.02 while maintaining low under-triage. These results support coupling LLM language understanding with executable clinical guidelines for triage from intake notes.

items.title: An Adaptive, Generative Framework for Continuous Multimodal Avatar Authentication in the Metaverse
items.abstract: Metaverse technologies let users interact inside virtual environments, where each user is represented by an avatar that carries their digital identity. These environments now attract many application domains, and these domains do not all need the same level of security. Conventional authentication methods do not fit them well. They ignore the continuity of user activity during a session and do not exploit the metaverse's rich set of interaction modalities, far broader than in 2D systems, through which an avatar continuously produces voice, head movement, gaze, and others. Moreover, they cannot adjust to different security levels within the same environment. Therefore, continuous, non-intrusive and adaptive authentication is needed. We first review existing avatar authentication approaches, organize them into three categories, and draw out the limitations a solution must address. Building on this, we propose an AI-driven continuous multimodal authentication framework for the metaverse. The framework reads behavioral biometrics from several interaction modalities and authenticates the user through their avatar without breaking immersion. The security level is continuously adjusted to the context of the session, using an adaptive control mechanism that weighs scene sensitivity, risk, and trust. A generative AI component builds context-aware authentication scenarios that adjust to the required security level and to the sensitivity of the scene. We evaluate the framework in two ways: a comparison against existing work, and a scenario-based analysis. The comparison shows that our framework integrates capabilities that previous approaches generally address separately, while the scenario-based analysis illustrates its intended operation and its internal consistency with respect to adaptivity and context-awareness.

items.title: An Analysis of Obstacles in Fulfilling Administrative Requirements for Marriage Registration by Prospective Brides and Grooms (A Case Study at the Office of Religious Affairs [KUA] in Tembalang, Semarang City)
items.abstract: This study aims to identify the obstacles faced by prospective couples in fulfilling the administrative requirements for marriage registration at the Tembalang Religious Affairs Office (KUA) in Semarang City, analyze the causal factors, and formulate appropriate solutions to overcome them. This research employed a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected through interviews, questionnaires, and observation involving 7 KUA staff members and 20 prospective couples. Data analysis was conducted using a descriptive-analytical method based on the Miles and Huberman interactive model, strengthened by triangulation techniques. The findings reveal that the main obstacles include incomplete N1–N5 documents, birth certificates, health certificates, parents’ marriage books, outdated identity cards and family cards, commander’s permission for TNI/Polri members, and guardian-related issues due to parental divorce. Contributing factors include limited information, prospective couples’ lack of thoroughness, processes at other institutions, and family-related problems. In addition, the poorly positioned physical information media and non-ergonomic spatial layout exacerbate information asymmetry. This study recommends strengthening public education, improving spatial layout, and optimizing information media to enhance the effectiveness of marriage registration services.

items.title: An artificial intelligence meta-skills framework for undergraduate research
items.abstract: Undergraduate research faces unprecedented challenges in the digital era, as exponentially growing data increasingly shapes the university ecosystem. However, artificial intelligence, particularly tools such as ChatGPT, offers significant opportunities to address this transformation. Effective use requires advanced competencies in generating, acquiring, storing, and analyzing data. In response, this study developed and validated a new Big Data Socio-Technical Competence Scale to assess undergraduate students’ competencies in research contexts. This study examined the relationship between Big Data socio-technical competencies and undergraduate students' academic use of ChatGPT, as well as the underlying meta-skills for using AI in research. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design (QUAN → qual) was adopted, involving 418 undergraduate students. We used two measurement instruments: the newly developed and validated Big Data Socio-Technical Competence Scale and a scale measuring the academic use of ChatGPT; both showed high internal consistency, along with a semi-structured interview protocol. The findings show that Big Data competencies were generally low, whereas the academic use of ChatGPT for research was predominantly medium to high. Structural equation modeling revealed that socio-technical competencies in Big Data positively and significantly predict the academic use of ChatGPT (β = 0.269, p < .001). The qualitative phase identified nine Artificial Intelligence Meta-Skills for Undergraduate Research: (1) Critical Data Literacy, (2) Critical Thinking, (3) Epistemic Data Management, (4) Evidence-Based Decision-Making, (5) Critical Data Communication, (6) Metacognitive Regulation, (7) Emotional Self-Regulation, (8) Responsible Human–AI Agency, and (9) Ethical Reasoning. The study discusses educational implications and practical applications.

items.title: An Improved Model for Occupational Health and Safety Risk Assessment Based on Consensus Analysis and MARCOS Approach
items.abstract: Occupational health and safety risk assessment (OHSRA) is a critical activity to identify and analyze the risk of occupational hazards for ensuring the safety of workers, and then take measures to control occupational risk at a tolerable level. In this study, an improved OHSRA model based on consensus analysis and the measurement of alternatives and ranking according to compromise solution (MARCOS) method is introduced to assess and prioritize the risk of occupational hazards under linguistic D numbers (LDNs) environment. First, the LDNs are employed to express the uncertain or hesitant risk assessments of occupational hazards provided by experts. Second, an improved minimum conflict consensus method (MCCM) is adopted to coordinate the conflict opinions among experts considering their conflicting degrees. Then, the MARCOS method is modified to determine the risk ranking of occupational hazards. Finally, an illustrative hospital-based application focusing on medical staff occupational hazards is presented to show the implementation procedure of the proposed OHSRA model. Sensitivity and comparative analyses are further conducted to examine the robustness of the results within this specific application context.

items.title: An ODeL-based teacher professional development framework for teacher-facilitated human–AI collaboration in primary mathematics problem-solving: a conceptual analysis
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly present in primary mathematics classrooms, yet their educational value is widely argued to depend on how teachers use them. Existing models explain parts of this problem: AI-TPACK describes the knowledge teachers need, teacher-in-the-loop and human-centred AI models describe how control is shared between teachers and systems, and orchestration research describes how teachers coordinate classroom activity. What remains under-theorised is the pathway linking the way open distance e-learning (ODeL) professional development builds teachers’ capacity to its enactment when AI scaffolds learners’ problem-solving. This conceptual article asks: through which mechanisms, and under which conditions, can ODeL-based professional development be expected to enable teacher-facilitated human–AI collaboration that supports primary learners’ mathematical problem-solving? The analysis combined an integrative review of peer-reviewed and selected grey literature with theory synthesis: sources were identified through structured database searches, screened against pre-specified criteria, coded for constructs, mechanisms and boundary conditions, and organised by level of analysis. The primary context is South African primary schooling (Grades 1–7) and low-bandwidth, predominantly asynchronous ODeL. Positioning four perspectives within a multilevel meta-model, Intelligent-TPACK at the teacher level, Zone of Proximal Development scaffolding and social constructivism at the interaction and classroom levels, and Polya’s heuristic as an analytic lens at the learner level, with transactional distance theory at the programme level, I propose a three-layer framework that distinguishes inputs, mechanisms, practices and outcomes, and derive seven testable propositions. These include teacher orchestration as a mediator between AI-TPACK and scaffolding quality; infrastructure readiness, learner age, language, and AI type as moderators; and governance and children’s rights as cross-cutting boundary conditions. Unlike models that specify teacher knowledge or the division of control alone, the framework specifies the professional development pathway through which human–AI collaboration is expected to benefit learners. I propose that well-designed ODeL professional development is an enabling condition for such benefit, not a guarantee of it, and close with implementation and evaluation indicators for teacher educators, policymakers, school leaders, researchers and learners.

items.title: ANALYSIS OF THE IMPLEMENTATION OF OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND SAFETY (OHS) MANAGEMENT AND SAFETY CULTURE ON EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE AT PT XYZ PURWAKARTA
items.abstract: This study aims to analyze the implementation of Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) management and safety culture in relation to employee performance at PT XYZ Purwakarta. Occupational Health and Safety is an essential aspect of industrial operations because it helps protect employees from workplace accidents, occupational hazards, and potential health problems. Effective OHS management also supports the creation of a safe, comfortable, and productive working environment. The implementation of OHS at PT XYZ includes the provision of appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), regular safety training for both new and existing employees, and routine supervision to ensure compliance with established Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). These measures are intended to increase employee awareness, reduce workplace risks, and encourage safe working practices. Furthermore, a strong safety culture plays an important role in shaping employee behavior and improving individual responsibility for workplace safety. Employees who understand the importance of safety procedures are more likely to comply with regulations, identify potential hazards, and contribute to accident prevention. However, the effectiveness of OHS management still requires continuous improvement, particularly through enhanced safety knowledge, consistent supervision, and greater employee participation in safety-related activities. Human negligence remains a potential risk factor that must be addressed through education, communication, and regular evaluation. Overall, effective OHS management combined with a positive safety culture can contribute to workplace safety, employee well-being, operational stability, and improved employee performance at PT XYZ Purwakarta

items.title: Anticipating street-flooding complaints through rainfall data: a Value-at-Risk approach for urban operations
items.abstract: Urban street-flooding is a growing concern in coastal cities, where intense rainfall and aging drainage systems often combine to disrupt daily life. This study introduces a value-at-risk (VaR) framework for anticipating resident-reported street-flooding complaints in New York City from antecedent rainfall. It draws on 15 years of publicly available 311 and weather-station data, with more than 75% of complaints occurred within two days of measurable rain. This finding motivates a rainfall-based approach to understanding complaint activity in three boroughs: Manhattan, Queens, and Staten Island. In each, total rainfall, peak hourly intensity, and recent rainfall history all meaningfully correspond to complaint volumes. Using an autoregressive negative binomial model, we estimate expected daily complaint counts and derive a calibrated VaR threshold that flags days with a high likelihood of unusually large complaint volumes. In Queens and Staten Island, the threshold is better calibrated than in Manhattan, though still somewhat conservative relative to the nominal risk level. Overall, these results demonstrate that publicly available rainfall data contain substantial information about street-flooding impacts as experienced and reported by residents. The proposed probabilistic, impact-based forecasting framework therefore provides a practical tool to support monitoring, planning, and early situational awareness.

items.title: Application of dynamic symbolic execution and test coverage enhancement combined with artificial intelligence in large-scale web software systems
items.abstract: Aiming at the bottleneck problems of path explosion and low efficiency of constraint solving faced by dynamic symbolic execution (DSE) in large-scale Web software systems, this paper applies a DSE and test coverage enhancement method combined with artificial intelligence (AI). Firstly, an Actor-Critic dual network model is constructed based on the PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) algorithm. The Actor network outputs the probability distribution of path selection, and the Critic network evaluates the value of path state. Secondly, the path priority sorting strategy is updated through the generalized advantage estimation and pruning mechanism, and the path depth threshold is gradually increased by combining curriculum learning. The key branch priority solving strategy is applied to optimize the efficiency of constraint solving. Finally, after each round of symbolic execution, the coverage increment is used as a reward signal to update the model parameters online and dynamically optimize the path exploration strategy. Experimental results show that this method significantly improves the efficiency of path exploration (the number of paths reaches 225 and 216, respectively) and test coverage (74.9% and 73.4%) on large-scale Web systems, with an average solution success rate of 79.8% and an average vulnerability detection rate of 88%. It has good vulnerability detection capabilities and resource adaptability, and provides an efficient and scalable new paradigm for automated testing of complex systems.

items.title: ARMS 2026: UTS TeamBuilder: AI and data driven insights for building cross-university collaboration
items.abstract: Universities have a wide range of expertise, but identifying the right people for complex, cross-disciplinary opportunities can be difficult. Expertise is often spread across faculties, research centres and different institutional systems. When funding and partnership opportunities have short response periods, those supporting team formation may rely on familiar networks and people with relevant but less obvious capabilities. UTS TeamBuilder is an AI-assisted tool that helps people find the right researchers, explore expertise across the university, and form teams around new opportunities. Rather than simply producing a list of names, the tool supports the broader team formation process, from framing the challenge and exploring institutional capability to preparing introductions and facilitating early conversations. The tool brings together evidence from multiple institutional sources, including researcher profiles, publication abstracts, research projects, proposals and staff bios. It uses natural language processing, network analysis, interactive visualization and generative AI to help users explore expertise, assess possible team combinations, and understand the evidence behind suggestions. Outputs can include expertise landscapes, preliminary team propositions, personalised invitations and prompts to support early team conversations. A key principle behind the tool is that AI should support, rather than replace, human judgement. Users can inspect the visualizations and analysis used by the AI, refine the researcher pool, explore proposed team members, and adjust the direction of the analysis. TeamBuilder therefore broadens the user’s field of view and provides informed starting points, while leaving decisions about team composition and suitability with the human user.

items.title: Artificial intelligence across the stone-associated urinary infection pathway: imaging, urosepsis prediction, and antimicrobial stewardship
items.abstract: Abstract Complicated urinary tract infection associated with urinary stone disease remains clinically challenging because obstruction, infected stones, delayed microbiological confirmation, and antimicrobial resistance may converge in the same patient. Artificial intelligence can support this pathway when it is framed as clinical risk integration rather than isolated image recognition. We conducted a structured narrative search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar from database inception to 31 July 2026, supplemented by reference chaining and relevant clinical and reporting guidelines. The synthesis distinguishes direct evidence in stone-associated infection and perioperative infectious outcomes from indirect evidence in stone detection, volumetry, recurrence, and general UTI stewardship. Radiomics and machine learning studies show promising discrimination, but the evidence remains predominantly retrospective and frequently lacks external validation, complete calibration reporting, and prospective impact assessment. Artificial intelligence should therefore be treated as an adjunct to urological assessment, cultures, imaging, antimicrobial stewardship, and timely source control. For African settings, pragmatic validation must account for local resistance patterns, uneven access to CT and microbiology, referral delays, infrastructure, and the availability of urgent drainage.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and digital transformation for sustainable supply chain performance
items.abstract: This study examines the nexus between digital technology adoption and Sustainable Supply Chain Management, focusing on their combined impact on sustainability performance. By bridging the domains of digital transformation and sustainability, the research advances a comprehensive conceptual framework that captures the effects of Industry 4.0 technologies, specifically the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, and blockchain, on sustainable supply chain outcomes. The proposed model posits that digital technology adoption enhances sustainability performance indirectly through improved supply chain transparency, with this relationship moderated by the presence of a skilled workforce. Grounded in a thorough review of contemporary literature, the study highlights the role of Industry 4.0 technologies in promoting eco-efficient production and logistics, the contribution of blockchain to strengthening transparency, and the optimization of resource utilization through AI. An empirical quantitative study based on survey data collected from 250 manufacturing firms provides evidence of the partial mediation effect of transparency and validates the moderating influence of human capital in reinforcing the relationship between digital transformation and sustainability. The findings offer novel theoretical insights into the mechanisms linking digital adoption to SSCM and yield practical implications for managers seeking to leverage Industry 4.0 technologies for sustainability objectives. The paper concludes by outlining directions for future research to further advance the digital–sustainability interface.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and doctrinal authority: Emerging ethical and theological questions for the Church in Ghana
items.abstract: This study examined the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) and doctrinal authority in the context of the Church of Ghana. The increasing use of AI in sermon preparation, biblical interpretation, theological research, and religious communication has raised important theological and ethical concerns regarding the integrity of Christian doctrine and the legitimacy of machine-assisted theological content. The study specifically explored how AI influences theological interpretation, the ethical issues associated with AI-generated religious content, and how churches should respond to AI-driven theological tools. The study was underpinned by Hermeneutical Theory and Technological Determinism Theory and grounded in the interpretivist paradigm. It used a qualitative research approach with a phenomenological research design. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with nineteen purposively selected participants, including pastors, church leaders, seminary lecturers, theological educators, and theological students. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed that AI is increasingly being used in sermon structuring, biblical explanation, theological research, contextual communication, and comparative doctrinal synthesis. However, the study also found that AI-generated religious content raises serious concerns related to doctrinal inconsistency, authorship and authenticity, overdependence, misinformation, and spiritual disconnection. The study concludes that while AI may serve as a useful assistive tool in ministry and theological education, it cannot function as a source of doctrinal authority. The paper recommends doctrinal oversight, digital theological literacy, and ethical guidelines for the use of responsible AI in Christian contexts.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Indian Labour Market: A Comprehensive Analysis of Employment Effects, Channels and Distributional Effects
items.abstract: Abstract: AI is flooding into India's job market faster than most legislative frameworks can keep up with. This review draws together nineteen peer-reviewed publications, working papers and institutional reports, mostly published between 2023 and 2026, in order to evaluate what is empirically known about the employment effects of AI in India, as opposed to what is anticipated or assumed. The review finds that empirical evidence is still concentrated in India's formal services sector, where AI-related hiring has skyrocketed since 2016 and appears to have reduced demand for high-skilled managerial and analytical roles rather than low-skilled ones. Most of the Indian workers are engaged in manufacturing, agriculture and the informal economy, all of which have little evidence largely based on projections and not empirical. The review categorises the literature based on four recurring mechanisms: task displacement, task reinstatement, productivity-driven labour demand and skill polarisation. Distributional data show AI exposure in India is stratified by caste, gender and educational attainment. The most urgent void in Indian literature is sector-specific, worker-level empirical research outside of IT services. items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Power Systems: A Review of Methods, Use Cases, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Modern electrical networks face growing operational demands as electricity consumption rises and renewable generation, distributed resources, and electric vehicles become more common. Artificial intelligence (AI) can learn useful relationships from operating records and simulated data, supporting tasks such as demand prediction, fault identification, state estimation, stability screening, and energy scheduling. This review organizes reported AI techniques and applications in both large interconnected grids and smaller power systems. It considers rule-based and fuzzy approaches alongside machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, and newer foundation-model methods. The literature suggests that AI may accelerate selected analyses and provide flexible decision support, but dependable performance still relies on representative data, generalization, explainability, cyber protection, and real-world validation. A staged approach that combines AI with engineering models and expert oversight is outlined. This paper synthesizes existing studies and does not claim new experimental results..

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Pregnancy, Childbirth, and the Postpartum Period: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Background: The use of digital health technologies, such as chatbots and virtual assistants based on artificial intelligence, has grown significantly in maternal health. These tools have been applied at different stages of the pregnancy and postpartum cycle, with emphasis on health education, risk monitoring, breastfeeding support, and mental health care. Despite their potential, challenges remain regarding clinical effectiveness, equity of access, and ethical safety. To describe, through a narrative literature review, the use of chatbots, conversational agents, and virtual assistants as support during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period, identifying applications, benefits, limitations, and perspectives for health practice. Methods: A narrative literature review was conducted between August and September 2025 in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Nursing Database, Latin American and Caribbean Literature in Health Sciences and Google Scholar. Original articles, reviews, experience reports, and theoretical reflections published in Portuguese, English, or Spanish that addressed the use of digital tools based on artificial intelligence in the pregnancy and postpartum cycle were included. The analysis of the studies was organized into five thematic axes: applications in prenatal care, support during childbirth, postpartum monitoring and breastfeeding, perinatal mental health, and ethical, technical, and implementation challenges. Results: The search identified 6,230 records, of which 13 studies were included. Findings indicate that chatbots and virtual assistants show good acceptability, promote health education, and contribute to the early detection of physical and emotional risks. However, most of the studies are exploratory, with methodological limitations, lack of clinical trials, and limited validation in socially vulnerable contexts. Conclusions: Chatbots and artificial intelligence tools are promising resources for perinatal care, particularly as a complement to face-to-face attention. Their consolidation requires robust studies, cost-effectiveness assessments, and public policies that ensure equity and digital inclusion.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Sustainable Development and Business Transformation: A Conceptual Study
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly positioned at the intersection of business transformation and sustainable development. Its capacity to identify patterns in large datasets, forecast demand and risk, automate routine processes, support product innovation, and improve resource allocation creates opportunities to enhance organizational performance while addressing environmental and social priorities. Yet these outcomes are not automatic: AI can reproduce bias, intensify surveillance, displace or transform work, widen digital inequalities, and consume substantial energy and material resources. This conceptual study synthesizes the supplied literature review on AI-enabled sustainability, digital transformation, innovation, governance, and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It develops an integrated framework in which AI capabilities influence sustainable business transformation through three complementary mechanisms: operational and resource optimization, innovation capability, and data-driven decision-making. The proposed framework links AI adoption with economic, environmental, and social sustainability through digital infrastructure, workforce skills, organizational readiness, and collaboration. Responsible governance, fairness, accountability, and data protection ensure ethical implementation. AI-driven sustainability requires strategic alignment, organizational learning, and responsible practices to achieve measurable business transformation and sustainable outcomes. As a conceptual paper, it does not claim empirical validation; instead, it offers propositions and a research agenda for future survey, case-study, and structural-equation modelling research.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence as an Assistant in Research Evaluation and Peer Review: A Critical Case for Augmentation Without Replacement
items.abstract: Peer review is important in maintaining the quality of scholarly publishing, but the process faces challenges such as shortage of reviewers, delays, inconsistent judgements, and overlooked errors. These challenges have increased the need to consider the appropriate use of artificial intelligence (AI) in peer review. Completely excluding AI or allowing it to function as an autonomous reviewer may not adequately address these problems. A Human–AI Augmented Review model is therefore proposed, in which AI supports clearly defined tasks under human supervision, while reviewers and editors retain responsibility for interpretation, ethical judgement, and editorial decisions. Peer review involves both routine technical checks and complex scholarly evaluation. AI can assist with repetitive and rule-based tasks such as manuscript screening, consistency checking, reviewer identification, and identification of reporting gaps. Human reviewers are still needed to assess methodology, scholarly contribution, and ethical issues. Effective use of AI requires a clear division of responsibilities, verification points within the review process, and governance measures to address bias, hallucinations, confidentiality, and excessive reliance on automation. Careful and limited use of AI can improve efficiency and reduce avoidable errors while maintaining accountability and trust in peer review.

items.abstract: Introduction: Gastrointestinal disorders involve interacting digestive, emotional, sleep, and behavioral factors requiring longitudinal assessment. Objective: To evaluate 12-week feasibility, engagement, and clinical associations of a mobile AI-driven mental health assistant in adults with gastrointestinal disorders. Methods: This prospective comparative study enrolled 186 Venezuelan adults with irritable bowel syndrome, inflammatory bowel disease, functional dyspepsia, or gastroesophageal reflux disease. Participants were assigned to a mobile AI assistant plus standard medical care (n=94) or standard medical care (n=92). The intervention combined conversational support, journaling, and emotional self-reports with required wearable-based monitoring (e.g., smartwatch and smart ring). Both groups underwent assessment of sleep, resting heart rate, nocturnal heart-rate variability, and daily steps. The primary outcome was symptomatic days per week. GAD-7 and PHQ-9 assessed anxiety and depression; adjusted differences included 95% confidence intervals. Results: Participant retention was 91.5% in the intervention group and 85.9% in the standard medical care group, with fewer symptomatic days, reduced anxiety and depression, and 28 additional minutes of sleep nightly. Resting heartrate decreased by 3.6 beats/min and nocturnal RMSSD increased by 5.1 ms relative to comparison; both confidence intervals excluded zero. Daily-step differences were nonsignificant. Daily check-in completion among enrolled participants was 74.8%. items.title: Artificial Intelligence Assisted Lifestyle Counseling in Preventive Cardiology a Clinician in the Loop Perspective
items.abstract: Lifestyle counseling is central to cardiovascular prevention, yet recommendations may be difficult to communicate within routine consultations and to translate into feasible daily actions. This perspective proposes a clinician supervised framework in which artificial intelligence helps draft patient readable lifestyle plans from explicitly approved clinical instructions. The framework separates deterministic safety rules and curated clinical content from language generation; a template system without machine learning is recognized as a valid alternative. Personalization is limited to clinician verified information and patient stated preferences, including language, food affordability, and practical access to physical activity. Proposed safeguards include data minimization, version controlled source material, documented review, patient clarification, and escalation when inputs are incomplete or conflicting. Particular attention is given to professional accountability, health literacy, digital exclusion, and the possibility that fluent drafts encourage superficial verification. Lifestyle advice is not assumed to be inherently safe, especially in patients with multimorbidity. This article presents a conceptual proposal rather than an evaluated intervention or systematic review. A staged research agenda compares the approach with high quality nonautomated counseling materials and measures safety, comprehension, clinician workload, equity, and sustained behavior change. Any benefit remains to be established empirically; the intended contribution is a testable model of accountable health communication rather than a claim of improved cardiovascular outcomes.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Attitudes and Readiness Among Undergraduate Nursing Students: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Purpose:This study examined undergraduate nursing students’ attitudes toward artificial intelligence and their readiness for medical artificial intelligence, as well as the factors associated with AI readiness.Methods: A descriptive, cross-sectional design was employed. Two hundred and fifty undergraduate nursing students at a nursing faculty in western Türkiye participated during the 2025–2026 academic year. Three instruments were administered: a Participant Information Form, the General Attitudes toward Artificial Intelligence Scale, and the Medical Artificial Intelligence Readiness Scale for Medical Students.Results: The Positive General Attitudes toward Artificial Intelligence Scale yielded a mean of 3.88 ± 0.66, the Negative General Attitudes toward Artificial Intelligence Scale 3.26 ± 0.87, and the Medical Artificial Intelligence Readiness Scale for Medical Students 74.29 ± 13.43. Academic year was significantly associated with AI readiness. One-way ANOVA showed significant differences across year groups (F = 3.450; p = 0.012; η² = 0.040), with fourth-year students scoring higher than second-year students. In the multiple linear regression analysis, both second-year (β = −0.156, p = 0.014) and third-year (β = −0.143, p = 0.024) students had significantly lower readiness scores compared with fourth-year students. A moderate positive correlation was observed between positive AI attitudes and readiness scores(r = 0.430; p < 0.01). Positive attitudes toward AI and self-reported computer skills emerged as the strongest independent factors associated with readiness.Conclusion: Nursing students displayed generally favorable attitudes toward AI, yet readiness levels varied across academic years. Attitude and readiness, while correlated, appear to be distinct constructs. These findings highlight the need for intentional, practice-oriented integration of AI competencies into undergraduate nursing curricula.

Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML), is increasingly proposed as a decision-support tool that can integrate anthropometric, physical, technical, psychosocial and match-tracking data. This paper presents a focused narrative review of verified peer-reviewed studies, prioritising 2019–2026 publications, that apply AI to talent selection, performance prediction, playing-position classification, athlete profiling and scouting. The review examines three connected themes: data sources (field tests, match and tracking data, psychosocial measures, maturation indicators and video), learning methods (penalised regression, tree ensembles, support vector machines, neural networks and unsupervised clustering), and validation and deployment practice. The literature shows that models reach moderate to high internal discrimination, with area under the ROC curve (AUC) values reported from about 0.58 to 0.96 in a recent systematic review, while very high accuracies are usually reported for small or augmented datasets without external validation. Most studies are male-dominated, soccer-dominated and single-club, and few report calibration, fairness audits or prospective testing. The review contributes a comparative analysis of representative studies, a conceptual athlete-to-decision architecture that links multi-source data acquisition, age- and maturation-aware modelling, calibrated and explainable prediction, human-in-the-loop decision support and external validation, and a prioritised agenda of research gaps and future directions.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cyber Defense: From Intelligent Threat Detection to Autonomous AI Agents
items.abstract: The article provides a comprehensive analysis of the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in cybersecurity, taking into account the latest technological trends of 2024–2026. The main possibilities of applying AI to protect information systems are studied: automatic detection of threats and anomalies, real-time incident response, prediction and prevention of cyberattacks, recognition of malicious code and phishing, and continuous learning and adaptation of defense systems. Particular attention is paid to the phenomenon of autonomous AI agents as a new stage in the evolution of intelligent cyber defense systems: practical cases of agentic incident triage and investigation systems (Microsoft Security Copilot), autonomous vulnerability discovery (Google Big Sleep), autonomous penetration testing (XBOW, PentestGPT), as well as the first documented case of an AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign are analyzed. The risks and challenges associated with the use of AI are considered: misuse of technologies by attackers, false positives and missed threats, vulnerabilities of machine learning models and agentic systems, and ethical and legal aspects. The necessity of a balanced approach combining automated AI systems with expert human control based on human-in-the-loop and human-on-the-loop models is substantiated.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Financial Analytics: An Integrative Review of Financial Modeling, Forecasting, and Financial Controls
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied across finance, including fraud detection, risk assessment, and forecasting, yet forecasting and internal controls are often governed in separate initiatives. This paper examines two pillars of AI use in finance: AI-driven financial modeling and forecasting, and AI-driven reconciliation within internal control over financial reporting (ICFR). The paper is based on a literature review of 23 academic, regulatory, and standards sources, including materials from the SEC, PCAOB, and COSO. The review indicates that the two pillars are interdependent: reconciled, well-governed data underpins reliable forecasting, and continuous reconciliation combined with predictive modeling can support pre-filing risk detection in SEC reporting. Model risk management, explainability, and human sign-off emerge as governance requirements common to both pillars. Building on these insights, the paper proposes a five-stage maturity framework that sequences AI-driven reconciliation ahead of predictive forecasting, together with shared governance practices. The findings suggest that managing forecasting and controls under a unified governance approach offers a coherent pathway for AI adoption in finance. items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Financial Services in India: Adoption, Risks, Regulation and the Future of Fintech Lending
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping India’s financial services sector, with fintech (digital) lending emerging as a key area of adoption. Built on the country’s large-scale digital public infrastructure, digital lenders increasingly deploy AI across the credit lifecycle. These tools promise to widen formal credit access for new-to-credit and thin-file borrowers, micro and small enterprises, gig workers and low-to-mid-income households. However, they also raise concerns about algorithmic transparency, explainability, discrimination, consumer protection, privacy and cybersecurity. India has no single AI-specific law and oversight instead follows the sector-led, “techno-legal” approach set out in MeitY’s India AI Governance Guidelines (2025), which channels oversight through regulators such as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). This report draws on structured interviews with industry leaders and technology vendors, together with a survey of 21 digital lending firms which are estimated to account for roughly 80% of digital lending volume in the country. The report maps trends in AI adoption, identifies operational and governance challenges, and assesses future trajectories. Firms see productivity gains but cannot yet attribute profitability to AI, which leaves the business case unproven even as investment intentions grow, particularly in collections and customer experience. The most significant risks are data quality, cybersecurity and dependence on third-party vendors. India relies on sector-led, principles-based oversight, and the RBI’s draft model risk guidance is not yet binding, so regulatory ambiguity persists. The central challenge is to extend governance outward to customers, vendors and data supply chains, as quickly as deployment advances.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Medical Education: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning, natural language processing, and generative AI, is rapidly transforming medical education, particularly anatomy, assessment, and simulation.Objective: To systematically review the applications, educational benefits, limitations, ethical concerns, and emerging trends of AI in medical education since 2023.Methods: A structured literature search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and major medical-education publishers for studies published from January 2023 to July 2026.Twenty-nine eligible studies were synthesised across seven thematic domains.Results: AI applications included large language models, anatomy education tools, virtual simulation, AI-assisted assessment, and personalised learning.Evidence suggests potential benefits in learning support, simulation, question generation, and anatomy education.However, concerns regarding accuracy, hallucination, bias, academic integrity, privacy, and inadequate AI literacy remain.Evidence for improved educational outcomes is still limited, with many studies being small, single-centre, or pilot investigations.Conclusion: AI is becoming an important component of medical education, with particularly promising applications in anatomy and pre-clinical teaching.Responsible integration requires faculty oversight, competency-based AI literacy, ethical governance, validation of AI-generated educational content, and stronger outcome-based research.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN SCHOOL COUNSELING: OPPORTUNITIES, RISKS AND PRINCIPLES FOR RESPONSIBLE USE
items.abstract: This article examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in school counseling and argues that AI-based tools should support, rather than replace, the professional work of school counselors. Drawing on an analytical review of international policy documents, professional standards, empirical studies and the legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan, the paper identifies four main areas of application: administrative and data-management support, academic and career guidance, early identification of students who may need help, and conversational agents for social-emotional support. Studies of mental health chatbots report short-term reductions in self-reported depressive symptoms among young adults; however, the overall quality of the evidence remains limited, safety has rarely been evaluated, and school-age children have seldom been studied. The article also discusses the key risks of AI use: breaches of confidentiality, algorithmic bias, inaccurate or harmful responses, and the weakening of the human relationship that lies at the core of counseling. Particular attention is paid to Uzbekistan, where the Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence Technologies until 2030 and the Law on Personal Data create both opportunities and obligations for schools. The paper concludes with practical principles for responsible use: human oversight, data protection, transparency, evidence-based tool selection, AI literacy for counselors, clear crisis protocols and linguistic and cultural adaptation.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence has shown strong performance on selected skin lesion classification tasks, but accurate image classification alone does not establish clinical benefit. Differences in data provenance, disease spectrum, evaluation design and human interaction complicate interpretation of published results. The main objective of the study was to critically examine representative evidence on artificial intelligence for skin cancer recognition, with emphasis on dermoscopic imaging, public datasets, diagnostic evaluation and clinical translation. A focused narrative synthesis was developed using targeted literature searches and verification of primary publications, dataset descriptors and reporting guidelines through 21 October 2026. This was not a systematic review or meta-analysis. No new model was trained and no patient-level data were analysed. Early retrospective studies established the feasibility of convolutional neural networks for selected diagnostic comparisons. Subsequent research demonstrated both potential benefits of clinician–AI collaboration and susceptibility to misleading support. Prospective multicentre evaluation provides stronger evidence of diagnostic performance, while showing clinically relevant sensitivity–specificity trade-offs. Public datasets support reproducibility but differ in imaging modality, diagnostic labels, reference standards and sampling. Class imbalance, related images across data partitions, skin-tone disparities, acquisition artifacts and distribution shift remain central concerns. Explanations may influence decisions differently depending on user expertise and the order of presentation. The evidence supports continued evaluation of AI as assistance for defined clinical tasks. Responsible translation requires independent validation, transparent reference standards, subgroup analysis, calibrated operating thresholds, and prospective measurement of patient and service outcomes. Comparative evaluation of the complete clinician–AI workflow should take priority over isolated claims of architectural superiority.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN TEACHING ENGLISH: OPPORTUNITIES, CHALLENGES AND PEDAGOGICAL IMPLICATIONS
items.abstract: The article examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in teaching English as a foreign language. It describes the main categories of AI tools currently used in language education, including large language model chatbots, automated writing evaluation systems, speech recognition applications, adaptive learning platforms and machine translation. On the basis of an analysis of international and Uzbek scholarly literature and normative documents, the article identifies how these tools can support the development of the four language skills, personalise learning and provide immediate feedback. At the same time, it discusses the risks associated with AI, such as factual inaccuracy, threats to academic integrity, data privacy concerns, excessive dependence on technology and unequal access. The authors argue that AI should complement rather than replace the teacher and offer practical recommendations for the responsible integration of AI into English lessons in the educational system of Uzbekistan.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Digital Economy: Features of Application and Development Prospects
items.abstract: The subject of research — features of application and development of artificial intelligence technologies, which are becoming key in the digital economy. The aim of the work is to determine the level and characteristics of development of artificial intelligence for different countries, as well as its dependence on the participation of state institutions and influence of constant generation of innovations. The article analyzes the state and structure of artificial intelligence market by different segments: by types of technologies, by deployment models, by solutions, by end-users, company size and geography. The work reveals the main trends of market development, identified and argued advantages and possible disadvantages of using these advanced technologies. The research methods include application of general science analysis and synthesis methods, classification and system, methods of grouping and comparison, economic analysis, as well as historical and comparative-legal methods. The results of the study showed that responsible adoption of artificial intelligence technologies becomes crucial for its positive impact on society. The growing demand for digital information technologies should lead to increased demands for accountability and transparency in the development of artificial intelligence technologies, to the development of a legal doctrine on its development at the international level. The findings of the study point to the need for proactive tools to regulate the legal framework of artificial intelligence, through which the process of developing and using artificial intelligence becomes dynamic and responsible, The use of artificial intelligence systems is synchronized with the global goals of social development.

items.title: Artificial intelligence methods for morphological analysis and diagnosis of bacterial and fungal leaf diseases
items.abstract: Abstract Bacterial and fungal leaf diseases frequently produce overlapping visual symptoms, complicating automated diagnosis and limiting the transferability of models across crops and field conditions. This review systematically evaluates artificial intelligence methods for the morphology-based detection and differentiation of these diseases. Following a PRISMA-based selection process, 95 records published between 2017 and 2026 were identified, of which 59 eligible studies were included. The survey covers the morphological characteristics that distinguish bacterial and fungal diseases, traditional image processing and machine learning approaches, deep learning and generative AI techniques, and publicly available datasets. It also critically compares the performance, advantages, and limitations of existing diagnostic approaches. The findings indicate that deep learning dominates the literature, particularly in fungal disease detection, whereas research on bacterial diseases and generative AI applications remains comparatively limited. Although convolutional and transfer-learning models generally demonstrated strong classification performance, comparisons across studies were constrained by differences in datasets, evaluation protocols, and performance metrics. The principal barriers to practical adoption include morphological overlap between infections, class imbalance, and scarcity of expert-annotated images of bacterial and early-stage diseases, reliance on controlled-background datasets, limited external validation, model complexity, and insufficient interpretability. Future research should prioritize pathogen-balanced multicrop field datasets, standardized reporting and cross-dataset evaluation, multimodal fusion of RGB images with spectral and environmental data, domain adaptation, validated generative augmentation, explainable models, and lightweight edge deployment. By connecting lesion morphology with methodological and dataset evidence, this review provides a structured roadmap for developing robust, interpretable, and field-ready plant disease diagnosis systems.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence- Powered Smart Safety Cap for Farm Workers Using Artificial Intelligence, IoT and Wearable Sensors: A Review
items.abstract: Farm workers operating in sugarcane fields, forests, tea plantations, and other areas with thick vegetation may encounter hazardous animals and insects that are difficult to notice before approaching them. Conventional precautions, including sticks, torches, protective footwear, and visual observation, offer limited capability for identifying concealed threats in advance. Delays in communication and access to medical assistance can further increase the risks associated with such incidents. Recent progress in Artificial Intelligence (AI), computer vision, thermal imaging, edge computing, Global Positioning System (GPS) technology, and the Internet of Things (IoT) provides opportunities to develop wearable systems for improved agricultural safety. This paper presents a focused narrative review of research relevant to an AI-enabled safety cap, covering animal recognition, snake detection, thermal-based wildlife monitoring, edge deployment, and IoT- supported alert systems. The reviewed approaches are discussed across three areas: sensing methods, including visible-light cameras, thermal sensors, and supplementary positioning or motion sensors; deep-learning techniques, including YOLO -based detectors, transformer architectures, lightweight models, and object tracking; and system designs combining local processing, offline data handling, and cloud connectivity. Published results indicate that some animal and snake detection models achieve approximately 92–98% on selected evaluation metrics, while one thermal wildlife detection approach reports 89.1% mAP50 with approximately 1.45 million parameters. Certain lightweight YOLOv8 models have also demonstrated processing rates of around 52–65 frames per second on Jetson -class hardware, although performance may vary across devices and experimental settings. Despite these advances, much of the existing research relies on fixed cameras, aerial platforms, or controlled datasets. Limitations include restricted species coverage, insufficiently documented datasets partitioning, and limited evaluation under real agricultural conditions. The reviewed evidence does not establish the field performance of an integrated, multi-camera, head-worn safety device incorporating behaviour analysis, battery endurance assessment, and emergency alert testing. To address these gaps, this paper outlines a conceptual worker-to-cloud architecture combining visual and thermal sensing, edge-based inference, multi modal warnings, optional GPS-enabled SOS communication, and systematic field evaluation. The review also identifies research priorities for developing a practical and reliable wearable safety solution for agricultural workers.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling and large-scale machine learning analysis of tumor delivery of nanoparticles in mice
items.abstract: Nanomedicine is a promising strategy for cancer therapy. However, the low delivery efficiency of nanoparticles (NPs) to tumors remains a challenge and hinders clinical translation. In this study, an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model was developed to predict NPs' tumor delivery efficiency (DE) based on the physicochemical properties and experimental strategies. First, a generic PBPK model was applied to describe NPs’ tumor kinetics, and six different tumor-related parameters were determined. Second, machine learning (ML) and AI models were developed for predicting the tumor-related parameters. Incorporating the ML-predicted parameters into the PBPK model, an ML-assisted PBPK model was developed to predict the tumor kinetics of NPs. This generic PBPK model was applied to simulate the tumor kinetics, in which 114 out of 152 datasets (75%) achieved the determination coefficient (R 2 ) of ≥0.75, and the overall R 2 was 0.92. Distribution (PT) and permeability (PATC) coefficients at the tumor site were the most important parameters in predicting tumor DEs. The deep neural network (DNN) model was the best-performing model and selected for tumor-related parameter estimations. Targeting strategy and surface charge were determined as the important features for predicting various tumor-related PBPK parameters. External validation was conducted using an in vivo experiment, and half of the predicted concentrations were within the two-fold error of the observed data. This model can serve as a complementary tool for predicting tumor kinetics prior to animal experimentation, helping identify promising NP formulations and potentially improving the success rate of drug delivery.
